column5: The AI product lifecycle: define the problem and metric, measure a baseline, then a loop of eval set, prototype, eval-driven iteration, hardening, gradual rollout and operation, with production failures fed back into the eval set.

Clients call an LLM gateway that routes either to managed APIs or to a KV-cache-aware router in front of self-hosted engine replicas scaled on queue depth, with GPU memory split between weights and KV cache.
Input, tool and output guards wrap the LLM outside the model, blocked or failed requests get a safe reply, and checks are ordered by cost from regex to small classifiers to an LLM judge.

A change to code, prompt, model or index passes unit and schema tests, a smoke eval, a full regression against production and a safety suite, then a canary with online evals that rolls back automatically on a quality breach.

Several apps call one LLM gateway that resolves a logical model name, holds provider keys and centralises routing, fallbacks, quotas, cost, caching, logging and guardrails in front of two providers and a self-hosted engine.
A sequence of client, server and engine exchanging a streamed response over server-sent events, the raw events on the wire, and a timeline showing streaming cuts the wait to the time to first token.

The LLM holds no credentials and sends tool calls across a trust boundary to a tool executor, which gets a scoped short-lived token from a credential broker to call the external API and returns results with secrets stripped.

Switching providers runs through a gateway abstraction, prompt porting, offline evals, shadow traffic, a 1 to 10 percent canary and a ramp to 100 percent with the old provider as fallback, alongside the share of traffic each stage serves.

An application reaches providers through a multi-zone gateway and health-checked breakers that fail over in order from the primary to the same model elsewhere, another provider, a self-hosted model and a cached answer, with the forgotten single points of failure and the availability math.

A multi-LLM pipeline where extract output is validated and retried, falls back to another extractor when retries run out, optional enrichment can be skipped, critical failures go to a dead-letter queue, and five 98 percent steps multiply to about 90 percent.
A trace waterfall for a refund request where a tool call fails with a 403, the final answer claims success, and an online faithfulness eval flags the answer and links it back to the failed span.

Evaluation-driven development: define criteria, build the eval set, baseline, change the system, re-run per slice, loop back on any regression, ship behind a flag, and turn production failures into new cases.

Red teaming starts from a threat model of jailbreaks, document injection, exfiltration, tool misuse and cost abuse, then runs manual and automated attacks, triages by severity, fixes, and re-runs every successful attack from a regression suite.

A RAG pipeline from question to retriever to generator to cited answer, with retrieval, generation and end-to-end metrics under each stage and a rule for telling a retrieval failure from a generator failure.

A simulated user with a persona and hidden goal converses with the assistant over several turns, then a judge scores the whole transcript on goal completion, turns to resolution, retention, consistency and correction handling.

Logs and documents become sampled and synthetic inputs with model-drafted labels; agreed labels are accepted, while disagreements and a random sample of agreements go to expert review, and both feed a golden set and calibrated judge.
Production traffic becomes traces that feed sampled checks and judges, user signals and drift monitors, which raise alerts per slice for human review that feeds the golden set.

Building an eval framework: define done, collect real inputs, then loop through reading outputs, one binary criterion per failure mode, code checks and judges, judge calibration, a per-slice CI gate and the same scorers in production.

Fairness monitoring runs daily label-free indicators and monthly outcome metrics per group into an alert with confidence intervals, then root cause, fix and re-audit, with a chart of overall error staying flat while one group's error doubles.

A pre-launch red-team programme: scope and exit criteria, manual then automated attacks, fix and verify in a loop until the criteria are met, then sign-off and CI, with the S1 to S4 exit criteria and the fix order.
